insights.headline: Gold holds near $3,883 after its worst week in months; Goldman cuts targets as Fed hike bets build
insights.summary: Spot gold ended the week near $3,883 after a roughly 4.5% weekly fall — its worst week in four months — as hot October inflation lifted bets on a December Fed hike and the dollar hit a 19-month high. Goldman Sachs cut its year-end gold forecast to $4,150 an ounce and its end-2027 forecast to $4,800, while GLD saw $1.53 billion of outflows in 30 days. In India, MCX gold held near Rs 1.37 lakh per 10 g, October gold imports fell 62% on the year, and the rupee steadied near 94.24 to the dollar as foreign inflows returned. Silver closed the week near $48.77 an ounce after breaking below $50.

trending.title: Fed hike bets drive the sell-off
trending.summary: October inflation has traders pricing a December Fed hike, lifting the dollar to a 19-month high and gold below $4,000 for its worst week in months. Goldman cut its targets; GLD is seeing outflows.

trending.title: Gold's custody map shifts east
trending.summary: Singapore opened a 500-tonne sovereign vault to foreign central banks, with tax relief from April 2027, as reserve managers look beyond London and New York for storage.

trending.title: India's imports slump as the rupee steadies
trending.summary: October gold imports fell 62% to $5.51 billion as high prices curbed buying, the trade deficit hit $39.88 billion, and the rupee steadied near 94.24 as foreign inflows returned.

trending.title: Silver slides below $50
trending.summary: Silver closed near $48.77 an ounce after breaking below $50, down more than 5% on the week, though a sixth straight annual deficit still underpins the market.

items.title: Gold posts steep weekly loss as Treasury yields rise, Fed tightening bets persist
items.summary: Spot gold steadied near $3,883 an ounce on Friday after Thursday's steep losses, but still ended the week sharply lower as hot US inflation, rising Treasury yields and bets on further Fed tightening weighed on bullion. Silver fell 2.6% to about $48.63. October producer prices rose 0.3% on the month, annual PPI hit 6.5%, and markets priced an 89% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike in December.

items.title: Goldman Sachs cuts year-end gold price target to $4,150/oz, 2027 target to $4,800/oz
items.summary: Goldman Sachs has cut its year-end gold target to $4,150 an ounce from $4,650 and its end-2027 target to $4,800 from $5,400, citing the Federal Reserve's hawkish shift and another expected hike in December. The bank still sees central-bank buying averaging 60 tonnes a month supporting prices, with support returning once the Fed starts cutting rates in the second half of 2027.

items.title: Rate-hike bets keep gold on track for worst week in four months
items.summary: Spot gold held near $3,880 an ounce on Friday, up 0.1% after briefly touching $3,923 on the US producer-price data, and stayed set for a weekly drop of about 4.5%, its worst week since early June. October producer prices rose 0.3% on the month, below the 0.4% forecast, and traders put December quarter-point hike odds at 91.4%. Silver fell 1.9% to $49.05 an ounce, also headed for a weekly loss.

items.title: Gold Price Slips to Key Support as Fed Rate Risks and GLD ETF Outflows Build
items.summary: Spot gold ended the week at $3,883, just above key support at $3,852, after falling more than 30% from January's $5,600 peak, as rising yields and Fed hike bets weighed. The SPDR Gold Shares ETF has seen $1.53 billion of outflows over the past 30 days, with December hike odds above 90%.

items.title: Gold Breaks Below $4,000 as Rising Yields Redefine the Macro Trade
items.summary: Spot gold slid below $4,000 on Thursday, closing at $3,870 after hot October inflation lifted bets on a December Fed hike; the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.16% and the dollar index pushed above 103, its highest since April 2025. Gold steadied near $3,883 on Friday, with central-bank buying — 321 tonnes in Q3, up 42% on the year — the main offsetting support.

items.title: Singapore Makes a $65 Billion Bet on the Future of Gold
items.summary: Singapore's central bank has opened its national currency vault, with room for 500 tonnes of gold, to foreign central banks and sovereign entities, with a tax waiver for wholesale gold services from April 2027. The move gives reserve managers a sovereign custodian in Asia alongside London and New York, as central banks spread holdings amid worries about reserve security.

items.title: India's October gold imports plunge 62.57% to $5.51 billion amid global price correction
items.summary: India's gold imports fell 62.57% from a year earlier to $5.51 billion in October, Commerce Department data showed, with prices below $4,000 an ounce; April-October imports were down 39.9% at $24.78 billion. The World Gold Council said gold may be nearing a temporary bottom after ending October at $3,913 an ounce, down 6.3% in the month.

items.title: Rupee outlook improves as foreign inflows return despite wider October trade deficit: Axis Bank
items.summary: The rupee's outlook has improved as foreign inflows returned despite October's trade deficit widening to $40 billion, Axis Bank Research says. Foreign investors bought nearly $6 billion of Indian equities in early November, and the bank sees the current account deficit contained near 1% of GDP, with the rupee at 94.24 to the dollar after touching 93.69 on November 11.

items.title: Silver (XAG) Forecast: Long-Term Support Levels in Focus as Rate Hike Fears Grow
items.summary: Spot silver closed Friday at $48.77 an ounce, down 2.6%, after breaking below $50 as rate-hike fears and a strong dollar weighed; December Comex silver settled at $49.12. FXEmpire's James Hyerczyk puts long-term support at $46.48, the 61.8% retracement of the all-time high, with the main trend down while silver stays below $53.73.

items.title: Silver's 6th Annual Deficit Masks a Surplus as ETF Selling Adds Supply
items.summary: Metals Focus and the Silver Institute now expect a sixth straight annual silver deficit of 35 million ounces in 2026, narrower than the 46.3 million ounces forecast in April. But silver funds are expected to release 45 million ounces over the year, flipping the balance to a 10 million ounce surplus. Coin and bar demand is forecast at 215 million ounces, down 2%.

items.title: Central Bank Gold Buying Surges 42% as Prices Dip Below US$4,000
items.summary: Central banks bought 321 tonnes of gold in the third quarter, up 42% on the year and the most since late 2024, World Gold Council data show, even as prices slid below $4,000. China and Poland led reported buying, while about 63% of official demand was unreported; purchases in the first nine months reached 675 tonnes.

items.title: Fed's Jefferson says he is taking his policy cues from inflation
items.summary: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said on Friday that, with the economy growing and the labour market stabilised, he is taking his policy cues from inflation — a signal read as leaning toward further rate hikes to bring price pressures under control. Jefferson gave no guidance on the timing or size of any move, unlike other policymakers who have backed bigger or faster hikes.

items.title: Gold oversold, but further fall to $3,750 likely: Mirae Asset Sharekhan
items.summary: Mirae Asset Sharekhan's Praveen Singh says gold, at $3,873 after breaking below $4,000, looks oversold but may fall further toward $3,750 support, and toward $3,600 if that gives way. Hot October CPI — 0.4% against 0.3% expected — has lifted December Fed hike bets, pushing the dollar index past 103 and the 10-year yield to 5.08%.

items.title: Oil and gold imports push India's October trade deficit to US$39.88 billion
items.summary: India's merchandise trade deficit widened to a one-year high of $39.88 billion in October as festive gold buying and higher oil costs lifted imports nearly 20% from September. Gold imports rose to $5.51 billion from $1.80 billion in September, while exports hit a record $49.47 billion.

items.title: India's current account deficit seen widening to USD 57 billion in FY27 on higher imports: ICICI Bank
items.summary: ICICI Bank expects India's current account deficit to widen to $57 billion, or 1.4% of GDP, in FY27, with the goods trade deficit at $380 billion. October's merchandise deficit hit a 12-month high near $40 billion even as exports rose 45% to a record $49 billion, and the bank expects gold imports to stay moderate.

items.title: India's forex reserves rise by $2.49 billion to $719.55 billion: RBI data
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves rose $2.49 billion to $719.55 billion in the week ended November 6, the RBI's weekly data showed, recovering after two straight weekly declines. The value of the RBI's gold holdings rose $2.21 billion to $104.80 billion.

items.title: Gold Price Jumps By Rs 1,300, But Rate Still Below Rs 1,37,000 On MCX
items.summary: Gold futures rose Rs 455, or 0.33%, to Rs 1,36,680 per 10 grams, after rising as much as Rs 1,362 to an intraday high of Rs 1,37,587. Silver futures fell Rs 750, or 0.42%, to Rs 1,77,974 per kg. Gold had risen 46% in 2026 before the recent correction, NDTV Profit reports.

items.title: Gold rebounds after sharp fall, silver lags: What should Indian investors watch
items.summary: MCX December gold rose 0.39% to Rs 1.36 lakh per 10 g as bargain hunting followed Thursday's slide, while silver eased 0.14% to Rs 1.78 lakh per kg; spot gold gained 1.1% to $3,918.59 an ounce.

items.title: Gold Prices Fall to Rs 1.40 Lakh Per 10 Grams as Post-Diwali Demand Weakens
items.summary: Gold fell Rs 2,500 to Rs 1,40,900 per 10 grams in Delhi on Friday, a fourth straight session of losses, as weak global cues and fading demand after Diwali weighed on prices. Silver fell Rs 3,500 to Rs 1,84,000 per kg. HDFC Securities' Saumil Gandhi cited soft retail demand, a stronger dollar and rising US yields.

items.title: Fading festive demand weighs on bullion trade
items.summary: Delhi gold fell Rs 2,500 to Rs 1,40,900 per 10 g, its fourth straight losing session, while silver shed Rs 3,500 to Rs 1,84,000 per kg, as post-Diwali demand faded and weak global trends weighed, the All India Sarafa Association said.

items.title: India's gem and jewellery exports jump 34% to $2.92 billion in October on festive demand
items.summary: India's gem and jewellery exports surged 34.01% year on year to $2.92 billion in October, from $2.18 billion a year earlier, per GJEPC data. In rupee terms shipments rose 44.71% to Rs 27,862.82 crore, led by gold jewellery, silver jewellery and lab-grown diamonds on strong orders ahead of the Christmas and year-end holiday season.

items.title: SGB 2018-19 Series III final redemption today: Investors to earn up to 348% return; check RBI fixed price, interest rate
items.summary: The RBI has fixed the final redemption price for Sovereign Gold Bond 2018-19 Series-III at ₹14,024 per unit as the tranche matures on November 13, 2026, eight years after issue. Holders who bought at ₹3,183 a gram gain about 341%, and online buyers at ₹3,133 up to 348%, before the 2.5% annual interest.
